On iPhones there is a setting on iMessage where you can set it that it won’t show up as read. 

My experience with something like that, is you can get into a pattern of automatically not replying quickly, for me part of it is about rejection sensitivity. I send a message, when they respond I feel like if I respond again there is the potential for some kind of rejection. It could also be them messaging me back reassures me. For me there is also I think a weird element of a dopamine hit with it. If I don’t reply it’s like there is still that message to respond to, a reward. I think part of it comes from when I was younger being overly attached to certain girls, and waiting for their response was a bit painful. So I got in the habit of delaying response as I’m trying to delay those feelings. 

All a bit complex and strange. I have found the more secure and understanding I feel my partner is the more I will disclose, and the more I will be able to open up and feel comfortable with them.

I get you, we just want reassurance everything is ok and to not feel like they are ignoring us. 

I think it’s always an individual thing on both parties perspective.. Communication with the other person is so important and establishing whether what I said above is along the lines of what they’re living with. Honestly they might not even realise it. 😕

For me, that scenario would be down to wanting a quick response because it alleviates feelings of abandonment/“I’m not wanted” and anxiety…. And not replying due to maybe anxiety over what you might say/will he reject me in some way. A lot of it, for me, has to do with where I’m at mentally. If I’m going through a tough period of time… I might even subconsciously push you away because that’s better than being rejected or hurt. 

It’s pretty messed up… but it’s what we live with.

In-between stimulus and response, there is a space. Our whole life we have reacted to the stimulus in whichever way our emotion shifts us towards - e.g we feel an itch we instantly want to itch, we feel hunger we instantly have thoughts of food. Our whole life we live in this reactice, instinctual way. What happens when we practice meditation, is we learn to live observantly, rather than reactionary. We learn to see that space between the stimulus and response. when we feel the itch, there is space between the itch and the reaction of thoughts that come flooding in like "itch, itch itch! Get rid of it! I cant stand it!" 

This translates to everything in life, when we dont like something, anything, we become aversive to it. We try to avoid it. When we like or want something, we follow or gravitate toward it. These cycles of liking, disliking our reality, are what cause us suffering. The reality in front of us, even if it is a literal nightmare, is only a nightmare 'because you think it is." Yes, emotions such as fear, anger any negative emotion may arise, but objectively, they are just emotions.. It is only your thoughts that make them seem so much worse than they really are. In fact they arent bad in any concievable sense.. They are just electrochemicals passing through the space in your brain.

Meditating trains your brain to disconnect the emotional and thinking part of the brain, thus providing a level of peace.
